svg.title: B-spline Policy inference on the NexArm
svg.desc: The cameras and the joint state go into an ACT-style regression network, as on the ACT page. Its head predicts 16 knots and their control points instead of 16 actions; together they define one cubic B-spline segment. The curve is a weighted sum of basis functions, each non-zero over only four knot spans, so a control point moves the curve only locally. The controller samples the curve at 100 Hz and can traverse it n times faster, a(nt). When the next segment arrives, it is entered at the point t-star that best matches the last executed action, so consecutive segments join without a jump.
svg.text: BSP predicts a curve, not a list of actions.
